note: The original describes only the alate (winged adult); there is no soldier or worker. Head length is measured from the mandible apex to the posterior margin, so it is not directly comparable with other species of the genus measured to the mandible base.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate head dark brown to nearly black, wider than long (to the base of the postclypeus), densely covered with long and short pale yellow hairs; fontanelle an indistinct spot in the broad depression between the eyes; antennae 15-segmented, gradually wider and longer toward the apex; compound eyes black, nearly circular, projecting, their distance to the lower margin of the head less than their diameter; ocelli deep-set, with a projecting upper margin, large and nearly circular, separated from the compound eyes by their long diameter (slightly less than their diameter in A. fumosus and A. ater); labrum pale yellow, elongate, widest in the middle; postclypeus pale brown, bilobed, projecting, twice as wide as long, posterior margin concave; mandibles yellow, chestnut brown to black at the apex, very long (0.7 mm), extending beyond the labrum, longer than in fumosus (left mandible 0.6—0.7 mm) and gracilis (0.45 mm) and with longer marginal teeth; pronotum dark brown, less than twice as wide as long, narrower than the head, deeply and angularly emarginate in the middle and anterior part, anterior margin concave, posterior margin convex, sides rounded and narrowed posteriorly. Wings grey, veins yellowish brown, costa darker; media slightly nearer the cubitus and farther from the subcosta, reaching the wing apex; cubitus not reaching the wing apex, with 10—12 branches or branchlets reaching the lower margin.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark brown to nearly black, wider than long (to the base of the postclypeus), densely covered with long and short pale yellow hairs. Fontanelle an indistinct spot in the broad depression between the eyes. Antennae pale brown, 15-segmented, gradually wider and longer toward the apex, densely covered with long pale yellow hairs; segment 1 long, cylindrical; segment 2 shorter, somewhat clavate; segment 3 shorter than segment 2, narrow, clavate; segment 4 longer and wider than segment 3; apical segment elongate, nearly oval. Compound eyes black, nearly circular, projecting, their distance to the lower margin of the head less than their diameter. Ocelli deep-set, upper margin projecting, large and nearly circular, separated from the compound eyes by their long diameter. Labrum pale yellow, elongate, widest in the middle, narrowing and rounded toward the apex, with long pale yellow hairs, shorter than the mandibles. Postclypeus pale brown, bilobed, projecting, twice as wide as long, posterior margin concave. Mandibles yellow, chestnut brown to black at the apex, very long (0.7 mm), extending beyond the labrum. Pronotum dark brown, less than twice as wide as long, narrower than the head, deeply and angularly emarginate in the middle and anterior part; anterior margin concave, posterior margin convex, sides rounded and narrowed posteriorly; densely covered with long and short pale yellow hairs. Posterior margin of meso- and metanotum concave. Legs yellow with brown. Wings grey, veins yellowish brown, costa darker, margins fringed, surface punctate; media slightly nearer the cubitus, reaching the wing apex; cubitus not reaching the wing apex, with 10—12 branches or branchlets converging posteriorly toward the lower wing margin; wing scales shorter than the pronotum. Abdominal dorsum slightly paler than the pronotum, densely covered with long and short pale yellow hairs. Measurements: alate body length 11—12 mm in males, 13.5 mm in females; dealate body length 6—6.5 mm in males, 7 mm in females; head length (from the mandible apex to the posterior margin) 1.55 mm; pronotum length 0.65 mm, width 1 mm; hind tibia length 1.25 mm; forewing length 10.75 mm, width 2.55 mm; left mandible length 0.7 mm; head width (between the eyes) 1.25 mm; eye diameter 0.27—0.3 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type locality La Ceiba, Honduras; the type is a female alate (USNM Cat. No. 25692); the description is based on a series of alates collected at the type locality on 19 May 1916 (month 5) by the American consul F. J. Dyer (Nos. 6655, 6664).
